_help: Copy this file to brief-gen.json beside brief-gen.py, or point BRIEF_GEN_CONFIG at it, and edit it. Every key is optional; a key left out or null takes the default the script's docstring names, and the defaults write briefs that name no build tool and no machine path. Keys starting with an underscore are comments.
_paths: `evidence_root` holds the three folders and defaults to EVIDENCE_ROOT, else the working directory; the three folders and `template` are relative to it unless absolute. The lanes folder holds one report per lane, titled `# Lane <token> (<item>): <topic>`; the briefs folder receives the briefs; the reviews folder is where a review brief tells the reviewer to write. `template` is the lane brief template the hostile-input line of a fix or notes brief points at.
_worktree: `worktree` is where a lane's worktree lives, with {token} filled in; when it is null, or names no folder, the report's `Worktree <path>` word is used. The base is the merge-base of the lane tip with `base_branch`.
_rules: `laws` names a file of standing rules the implementer reads; null leaves the sentence out. `subject_suffix` is what every commit subject must end with, for example [skip ci] when the CI runs only before a merge; empty asks for nothing.
_commands: Templates filled per brief: {worktree} as written, {worktree_posix} in /c/... form, {worktree_native} in C:/... form, {tag} the run tag the brief picks (<token>-fix1, <token>-notes) and {tests} the --tests argument. `own_tests_command` runs the lane's own test classes on its committed tip, for example `bash scripts/run-own-tests.sh {worktree_posix} {tag} '{tests}'`; null writes a placeholder the orchestrator fills. `own_tests_done` is the file that run writes when it ends, for example {worktree_posix}/build/runs/{tag}.done; when set, the brief tells the lane to launch the run as a foreground call that returns at once and end its turn on that path instead of waiting. `precheck_command` is a static check of the new tip run after the tests; null leaves the line out. Write a literal brace as {{ or }}.
